directAnswer: Pope Paul III was Alessandro Farnese, who reigned from 1534 to 1549. He opened the Council of Trent in 1545, approved the Society of Jesus in 1540, established the Roman Inquisition, and named Michelangelo chief architect of St. Peter's, setting the Catholic Reformation in motion.

paras: Alessandro Farnese was born in 1468 into a noble family of the Papal States and received a humanist education, partly in the circle of Lorenzo de' Medici in Florence. Alexander VI made him a cardinal in 1493; the advancement was widely linked to his sister Giulia's closeness to that pope.

Before his priestly ordination he fathered several children, including Pier Luigi Farnese. He later reformed his life and became a respected senior cardinal. Elected unanimously in October 1534, he was then the dean of the Sacred College.

sections.h2: Reform Commission, Jesuits, and the Roman Inquisition
paras: Paul III raised reform-minded men to the cardinalate, including Gasparo Contarini, Reginald Pole, Gian Pietro Carafa and John Fisher, who was executed by Henry VIII weeks after his appointment in 1535. In 1537 a commission of these reformers delivered a frank report on abuses in the Church, the Consilium de emendanda ecclesia.

On 27 September 1540 the bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae approved the Society of Jesus founded by Ignatius of Loyola. In 1542 Paul III established the Congregation of the Roman Inquisition to oppose Protestant teaching in Italy, and in 1544 he approved the Ursulines. In 1537 he had also issued Sublimis Deus, affirming that the native peoples of the Americas were rational human beings who must not be deprived of liberty or property.

After years of negotiation with Charles V and Francis I, the Council of Trent opened on 13 December 1545. In its first sessions it defined the canon of Scripture, affirmed the role of Tradition, and issued a major decree on justification.

In 1547 Paul III moved the council to Bologna, partly over plague and partly over tension with the emperor, and its work stalled. Meanwhile he carried out the final sentence of excommunication against Henry VIII in 1538, following the dissolution of England's monasteries.

sections.h2: Michelangelo, St. Peter's, and the Farnese Family
paras: Paul III had Michelangelo complete the Last Judgment in 1541, and in 1546 appointed him chief architect of St. Peter's, where he designed the great dome. Michelangelo also redesigned the Capitoline Hill and worked on the Palazzo Farnese. Titian painted the pope's famous portraits.

Paul III did not escape nepotism. He made two teenage grandsons cardinals and in 1545 created the duchy of Parma and Piacenza for his son Pier Luigi, who was assassinated two years later. The pope died on 10 November 1549, having launched the reform that would define the Church for centuries.

keyFacts: Born Alessandro Farnese in 1468; cardinal from 1493
Approved the Society of Jesus on 27 September 1540
Issued Sublimis Deus on the rights of Indigenous peoples (1537)
Opened the Council of Trent on 13 December 1545
Appointed Michelangelo chief architect of St. Peter's (1546)

faqs.question: Did Paul III approve the Jesuits?
faqs.answer: Yes. On 27 September 1540 his bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally approved the Society of Jesus founded by St. Ignatius of Loyola and his companions.

faqs.question: What was the Consilium de emendanda ecclesia?
faqs.answer: A 1537 report by a commission of cardinals and prelates appointed by Paul III that candidly listed abuses in the Church, especially in the Curia, and proposed remedies.

faqs.question: What was Sublimis Deus?
faqs.answer: A 1537 bull of Paul III declaring that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas were true human beings capable of receiving the faith who must not be enslaved or robbed of their property.
